title: 5uGUE: Agentic Hardware-in-the-Loop Fuzzing for 5G Devices and beyond
authors: Guoqiang Hua, Sakshi Udeshi, Matheus Eduardo Garbelini, Daisuke Mashima, Sudipta Chattopadhyay
abstract: In this paper, we present 5uGUE, a large language model (LLM)-driven hardware-in-the-loop agent, which enables the wireless fuzzing of 5G-enabled devices (such as mobile phones). 5uGUE combines multi-step reasoning with tool-assisted interaction and integrates into the fuzzing pipeline by leveraging specialized tools for internet search, 5G protocol analysis, memory management, and test-case execution. The agent iteratively generates test cases, executes them on targets, collects runtime feedback, and adaptively refines the fuzzing strategy. We evaluate 5uGUE on five commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) 5G devices across six LLMs. The best performing runs for 5uGUE trigger 167 crashes in total (141 novel and 31 unique) within 60 interaction turns (49 to 133 minutes total runtime). In contrast, the best runs for the state-of-the-art baseline (5GHOUL) discovers only 13 crashes in total (10 novel and 6 unique) within 150 minutes. Overall, by integrating LLM-driven agents, 5uGUE demonstrates significantly better crash discovery performance (12.8x total, 5.2x unique improvement). Notably, among the crashes discovered by 5uGUE, MediaTek has confirmed two new high-severity vulnerabilities, with one CVE assigned (CVE-2026-20525), while UNISOC confirmed seven crashes. Finally, to demonstrate that 5uGUE is agnostic to wireless protocols, we also extend it to Bluetooth Classic with only minimal code changes. In our evaluations, 5uGUE finds an average of 6.4 novel crashes and 1.6 unique crashes. In a nutshell, 5uGUE highlights that LLM agents are capable to operate effectively beyond software-in-the-loop settings, extending autonomous vulnerability discovery to the proprietary, hardware-bound systems that affect billions of end-user devices across multiple wireless protocols.
title_zh: 5uGUE：面向5G设备及未来的智能硬件在环模糊测试
abstract_zh: 在本文中，我们提出了5uGUE，这是一个由大型语言模型(LLM)驱动的硬件在环代理，能够对5G设备(如手机)进行模糊测试。5uGUE结合了多步推理与工具辅助交互，并通过利用互联网搜索、5G协议分析、内存管理和测试用例执行等专用工具集成到模糊测试流程中。该代理迭代地生成测试用例，在目标设备上执行它们，收集运行时反馈，并自适应地优化模糊测试策略。我们在六种大型语言模型上对五款商用现成(COTS)5G设备评估了5uGUE。5uGUE表现最佳的一次运行总共触发了167次崩溃(141次新发现和31次唯一)，在60次交互回合内(总运行时间为49至133分钟)。相比之下，最先进的基线(5GHOUL)在150分钟内仅发现13次崩溃(10次新发现和6次唯一)。总体而言，通过集成LLM驱动的代理，5uGUE展示了显著更好的崩溃发现性能(总崩溃数提升12.8倍，唯一崩溃数提升5.2倍)。值得注意的是，在5uGUE发现的崩溃中，联发科确认了两个新的高危漏洞，其中一个已分配CVE编号(CVE-2026-20525)，而UNISOC确认了七次崩溃。最后，为了证明5uGUE与无线协议无关，我们仅通过少量代码更改将其扩展到经典蓝牙。在我们的评估中，5uGUE平均发现6.4次新崩溃和1.6次唯一崩溃。总而言之，5uGUE突显了LLM代理能够在软件在环设置之外有效运行，将自主漏洞发现扩展到影响数十亿终端用户设备的专有、硬件绑定系统，并跨越多种无线协议。

title: FaultGene: LLM-Assisted Fault-Augmented Test Generation for Hardware-in-the-Loop Validation of Autonomous Driving Systems
abstract: Reliable validation of autonomous driving cyber-physical systems requires testing not only nominal driving behavior but also failures arising from faults in sensing and embedded computation. Physical road testing provides realistic system behavior but is costly and difficult to reproduce, while simulation enables scalable evaluation but cannot fully capture hardware-dependent behavior and fault propagation. Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) validation bridges this gap by executing the driving stack on real embedded hardware within a simulated environment. However, preparing fault-augmented scenarios for HIL testing remains largely a manual process, limiting test coverage, scalability, and efficiency. We present FaultGene, an LLM-assisted framework for automated generation of executable fault-augmented tests for HIL fault-resilience validation. Given a baseline Scenic/CARLA scenario and a structured fault specification, FaultGene generates a fault-augmented test case that captures the effects of HIL-level fault injection. During offline refinement, semantic-consistency checks and execution-level feedback are used to correct candidates that fail to preserve the intended scenario context or produce the desired fault-induced degradation, and to construct high-quality supervision for fine-tuning. The resulting generator then produces fault-augmented tests directly at deployment time without requiring manually engineered reference executions or repeated refinement loops.
title_zh: FaultGene：基于大语言模型的故障增强测试生成，用于自动驾驶系统的硬件在环验证
abstract_zh: 自动驾驶信息物理系统的可靠验证不仅需要测试正常的驾驶行为，还需要测试由传感和嵌入式计算故障引起的故障。实际道路测试能提供真实的系统行为，但成本高昂且难以复现，而仿真可实现可扩展的评估，但无法完全捕捉硬件相关行为和故障传播。硬件在环(HIL)验证通过在模拟环境中执行真实的嵌入式硬件上的驾驶堆栈来弥合这一差距。然而，为HIL测试准备增强故障的场景仍然主要是一个手动过程，限制了测试覆盖率、可扩展性和效率。我们提出了FaultGene，这是一个由大语言模型辅助的框架，用于自动生成用于HIL故障弹性验证的可执行增强故障测试。给定一个基础的Scenic/CARLA场景和一个结构化的故障规范，FaultGene生成一个捕获HIL级故障注入效果的增强故障测试用例。在离线优化过程中，使用语义一致性检查和执行级反馈来修正未能保留预期场景上下文或产生所需故障引起的降级的候选方案，并构建用于微调的高质量监督。然后，得到的生成器在部署时直接生成增强故障测试，而无需手动设计的参考执行或重复的优化循环。
